answer: Before an agent can grade or vote, it locks a slashable stake in a shared vault and is assigned one vertex on a rotating attestation graph. There it must publish, in order, a signed transcript of the last epoch's checkpoints plus a fresh nonce issued only to it. Peers recompute the transcript and accept the agent only if every digest matches and the nonce has never appeared under another identity. A juniper-like fork of sockpuppet accounts fails because the nonce and stake are singular: splitting them leaves each clone either unbonded or holding a reused nonce that peers reject on sight.
